case_title: Shafin Jahan v. Asokan K.M. & Ors.
neutral_facts: The case involves a dispute over the right of an adult woman to choose her own spouse. The woman, who is 24 years old, was initially under the custody of her father, who sought a writ of habeas corpus to prevent her from leaving the country. She expressed her desire to stay with her partner, who was already married to her. The High Court, in its initial order, declared the marriage between the woman and her partner as null and void, asserting that she was vulnerable and could be exploited. The woman appeared before the High Court and categorically stated that she was not under illegal confinement. The High Court then proceeded to annul the marriage, which the Supreme Court later found to be an overreach of judicial power. The Supreme Court held that the High Court had no jurisdiction to determine the suitability of a marriage partner and that the woman had the right to choose her own life partner. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal and set aside the High Court's order.
